prompt: Create a map of Europe in 1914 immediately before the First World War. Show national borders and label the major states, including the German Empire, Austro-Hungarian Empire, Russian Empire, Ottoman Empire, France, United Kingdom, Italy, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Greece, Belgium, and the Netherlands. Distinguish the Triple Entente and Central Powers with a legend.

spec.title: Europe in 1914: Alliances on the Eve of World War I
spec.subtitle: National Borders and Major Powers, July 28 1914

sources.title: American Geographical Society Library: Europe 1914 Map
GHDI: Germany and Europe in the First World War
Library of Congress: World War I Declarations

notes: Borders reflect the political geography of Europe on July 28, 1914, the day Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia.
Alsace-Lorraine is shown as part of the German Empire (ceded by France in 1871).
Bosnia-Herzegovina is shown as part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire (annexed in 1908).
Poland is divided between the German Empire, Austro-Hungarian Empire, and Russian Empire.
The Ottoman Empire joined the Central Powers on October 29, 1914, but is shown as part of the alliance for context.
Neutral states are labeled as such, though some (e.g., Belgium, Italy, Romania) later joined the war.
spec.referenceSummary: Based on authoritative historical and cartographic sources, including HistoGIS, the American Geographical Society Library, and the Library of Congress.
